req.title: Reject wrong method on /patch
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PATCH on /patch.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /patch must accept PATCH and reject all other HTTP methods with 405. I design: (1) a positive test confirming PATCH returns 200 with expected JSON keys, (2) negative tests for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE each expecting exactly 405, (3) a boundary/decision-table test covering the full set of disallowed methods systematically. Each test asserts exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations (== vs !=, 200 vs 405). The positive test also asserts JSON payload keys to catch mutations that alter the handler's return value. Multiple disallowed methods are tested individually to catch any method-specific branching mutations.

tests.name: test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-009: PATCH on /patch must succeed with 2xx
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    r = client.patch('/patch')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in body

test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload()

tests.name: test_all_disallowed_methods_return_exactly_405_not_200_or_other
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE are all disallowed on /patch
actions: Iterate over disallowed methods and assert each returns exactly 405
Assert none of the disallowed methods return 200
expected: No disallowed method returns 200 or any other code
trace: R-HTTPBIN-009: boundary between allowed (PATCH=200) and disallowed (all others=405)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_disallowed_methods_return_exactly_405_not_200_or_other():
    disallowed = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('DELETE', client.delete),
    ]
    for method_name, method_fn in disallowed:
        r = method_fn('/patch')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"{method_name} should be 405, got {r.status_code}"
        assert r.status_code != 200, f"{method_name} must not return 200"
        assert r.status_code != 404, f"{method_name} must not return 404"

test_all_disallowed_methods_return_exactly_405_not_200_or_other()

tests.name: test_patch_with_body_returns_200_and_reflects_data
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
PATCH request carries a JSON body
actions: Send PATCH to /patch with JSON content-type and body
Assert response JSON field 'json' reflects the sent payload
expected: Response body JSON key 'json' equals the sent object
trace: R-HTTPBIN-009: positive path with payload; verifies handler processes PATCH body
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_patch_with_body_returns_200_and_reflects_data():
    payload = {"key": "value", "num": 42}
    r = client.patch(
        '/patch',
        data=json.dumps(payload),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['json'] == payload
    assert body['json']['num'] == 42
    assert body['json']['key'] == 'value'

test_patch_with_body_returns_200_and_reflects_data()
